english.title: Owner / user / person responsible for conduct of watercraft contravene the Merchant Shipping regulations
english.standardoffencewording: On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) **(..SPECIFY DETAILS OF THE OFFENCE..)
english.legislation: Contrary to Schedule 2 to the Merchant Shipping (Watercraft) Order 2023 and regulation 6 of the Merchant Shipping (Distress Signals and Prevention of Collisions) Regulations 1996.
english.pointstoprove:
date and location
owner/user/person responsible for conduct of watercraft
contravened
a provision of the Merchant Shipping (Distress Signals and Prevention of Collisions) Regulations 1996

investigatoraction.description: DNA Samples: If crime scene stain present - take evidential sample If no crime scene stain and DNA not confirmed on PNC - take Criminal Justice sample. If DNA confirmed on PNC - CJ sample not required
Confirm proposed charge is appropriately authorised (Police or CPS)
Ensure compliance with investigator's obligations re disclosure
Consider if case suitable for referral to Financial Investigation Unit and CPS for asset recovery eg confiscation order

english.notes:
(i) Schedule 2 to the Merchant Shipping (Watercraft) Order 2023 provides that the Merchant Shipping (Distress Signals and Prevention of Collisions) Regulations 1996 apply to watercraft as they apply to ships.
(ii) Regulation 6(2) of the Merchant Shipping (Distress Signals and Prevention of Collisions) Regulations 1996 provides a defence.
(iii) Regulation 7 contains a power to detain a ship.

other.penalty:
Either way
Summary: a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
Indictment: maximum 2 years imprisonment and/or a fine.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
